answer: Karst Percolation Proof: each identity publishes its capability graph; each epoch a VRF seeds a random query at a leaf vertex, and the agent must route a signed derivation to the graph kernel within bounded hops, the way a river finds its course through karst rock. Isolated sinkholes - vertices with no path to the kernel - void their shard's weight as fabricated skills. Clone farms bolt together a thousand disjoint one-vertex graphs, so random probes hit dead ends and percolation collapses; a real agent's graph stays connected because its expertise interlinks.
